Everything else — hooking, measuring, recording — works without it.

data.name: Settings_Interval_Body
data.value: How often hardware telemetry is sampled during a session (500–2000).

data.name: Settings_OnlineMetadata_Body
data.value: Off by default. FrameLedger sends no telemetry and makes no network call except the update check, the detection-rules fetch, and — only with this on — store metadata for your games. Nothing about your sessions ever leaves this machine.

data.name: Settings_RemoveUninstalled_Body
data.value: A game whose executable has been gone for ten minutes, from a drive that is connected, is removed from the library — only when it has no sessions, and never one where anti-cheat was found. Off, it stays and reads Not installed.

data.name: Settings_RemoveUninstalled_Applied

data.name: Settings_DeleteSessions_Body
data.value: Every session of every game, with its frame and sensor data and its notes. The library, your settings and each game's hooking consent stay. It cannot be undone.

data.name: Settings_Retention_Body
data.value: Per-frame data of the newest sessions is kept; older sessions keep their aggregates. 0 keeps everything.

data.name: Settings_SafetyDocs

data.value: Automatic follows this copy: a pre-release looks for pre-releases, a release for releases. Or choose Stable, or Beta (stable plus pre-releases). A found update downloads in the background and is applied only when you restart — never while a game is hooked.

data.name: Settings_VkLayer_NotRegistered
data.value: Not registered. Vulkan games launched from FrameLedger are measured through a per-launch manifest; registration is a repair tool, not the normal path.

data.name: Settings_VkLayer_Unknown

data.name: Settings_VkLayer_Note
data.value: Registration puts the layer into every Vulkan process of this user, where it stays inert unless FrameLedger launched that process. Launching from FrameLedger needs no registration. The capture agent registers the layer on its own while a hook-enabled game references the Vulkan loader and removes it when the last one is disabled; the buttons repair that state and are allowed only under the same rule.

data.name: FirstRun_Agent_Body
data.value: FrameLedger starts a small capture agent beside itself, as a standard user — not elevated. Elevation is optional and is not required by any capture tier: it only unlocks CPU temperature and, with Advanced metrics on, the processor's, the memory's and the motherboard's sensors (both through PawnIO), and attaching to games that run elevated themselves. Below is what the agent reports about this machine.

data.name: FirstRun_Explainer_Intro
data.value: FrameLedger measures a game by loading a library into its process — hooking. Hooking is off for every game until you enable it for that game, one at a time, after a dialog that repeats what is written here. The Disclaimer you accepted states the risk; this screen states what each choice records.

data.name: FirstRun_Explainer_Off
data.value: Nothing changes until you add a game and enable hooking for it. Every game you add starts with hooking off.

data.name: FirstRun_Import_Body
data.value: FrameLedger can read what Steam, GOG Galaxy, Epic, itch.io and the Xbox app have installed and add them from a checklist — File ▸ Import library…, once you are in. Every imported game starts with hooking off, exactly like one you add by hand.

data.name: FirstRun_Legal_Body
data.value: Three documents describe what this software does, what it does not do, and what it may cost you; Accept covers those three. The GNU GPL v3 is shown too: it is your licence to FrameLedger and needs no acceptance. Declining closes FrameLedger.

data.name: Maintenance_Intro
data.value: Your sessions live in one SQLite file, the ledger. Checking and backing up only read it. Compacting rewrites the file with the same contents and waits until no session runs. Sweeping removes raw series by your retention setting; the Agent does it, because those rows are the Agent's.

data.name: Maintenance_Backup_Body

data.name: Maintenance_Backup_IsLedger

data.name: Maintenance_Sweep_NoAgent

data.name: Maintenance_Sweep_AgentTooOld

data.name: FirstRun_Legal_Summary
data.value: In short — please read before you accept: • This is a beta (pre-release). It certainly still has bugs, and the developer is not responsible for problems that result. • Your PC must meet at least the minimum requirements the game's developer or publisher states. Read them first. Problems on a PC below them are your responsibility, not FrameLedger's. • Hooking loads a component into a game, one game at a time, only after you agree. Anti-cheat systems can ban an account for that, and a ban can come days later. FrameLedger refuses where it detects anti-cheat and turns hooking off for that game; the only exception is one you can make yourself, per game, for anti-cheat that runs entirely in user mode — and the risk is then yours. • Your recordings stay on this PC, and backing them up is up to you. The only network requests are the update check and download, to GitHub; the check can be switched off. The documents below are the full terms; this summary does not replace them.

data.name: Settings_PlayMode_Body
data.value: Through the store: Steam and the Epic Games Launcher start the game, GOG GALAXY runs it, the itch app asks first; a game no store installed is started by FrameLedger. Directly: FrameLedger starts the game itself — recorded from its first frame, with your standard rights. Some Steam games hand themselves to Steam when started directly — the game Steam then starts is recorded — and a few will not start outside Steam at all: start those through the store. A game from the Xbox app or the Microsoft Store always starts through Windows, as its Start-menu tile does, in either mode.
